 Appearance:
 Mr Apurva R Kapadia(5012) for the Petitioner(s) No. 1
 Mr Jit Jotangiya Agp for the Respondent(s) No. 1,2
 ==========================================================
 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Aniruddha P. Mayee
 Date : 06/10/2025
Oral Order

1. By the present writ petition, the petitioner prays for a direction to restore the reference application preferred by the petitioner under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ["Act, 2013" for short]
in L.A.R. No.1 of 2016.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ["Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Dy. Collector and Special Land Acquisition Officer by the impugned order dated 30.09.2024 has filed the application of the petitioner on the ground that requisite court fees has not been paid.

2. Learned advocate for the petitioner submits that the acquiring body does not have any power to reject the reference filed under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12952/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/10/2025 undefined on the ground of non-payment of court fees.
He submits that the amount of court fees in the present case was never determined by the authority and therefore also, the impugned order requires to be quashed and set aside.

He submits that the non- payment of court fees does not render the reference of the petitioner liable for rejection as the appropriate authority while dealing with the reference case can always pass a decree Vaghela Jenubha Jasmatsang vs State Of Gujarat on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149947179/
1 after deducting the amount of court fees.

entities.text: Vaghela Jenubha Jasmatsang vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that therefore, the impugned order requires to be quashed and set aside and the reference application of the petitioner be restored.

2.1 In support of his contention, learned advocate for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment of this Court in Karsanbhai Bhagwanbhai & Ors. v. Dy. Collector and Special Land Acquisition Officer,
Narmada - 2011 (3) GLH 702.

entities.text:
Karsanbhai Bhagwanbhai & Ors. v. Dy. Collector and Special Land Acquisition Officer,
Narmada - 2011 (3) GLH 702
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the respondents submits that despite repeated reminders to the petitioner by the respondent No.2, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12952/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/10/2025 undefined the petitioner has failed to pay the requisite court fees.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 had no option, but to file the application of the petitioner.

He submits that the State Government has issued standing instructions that in case any reference is filed without payment of court fees then after due intimation to the claimant if no court fees is paid then such applications are to be filed.

He submits that in accordance therewith, the respondent No.2 has passed the impugned order dated 30.09.2024.
4.
Heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the documents on record.
5. In the present case, it is admitted position that the reference application under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 has been filed by the petitioner within time.
Further, the respondent No.2 called upon the petitioner to pay court fees within a stipulated time.

Thereafter, several reminders were also issued,
however, the petitioner did not comply with the same and therefore, by the impugned order, the reference application of petitioner under Section 64 of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12952/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/10/2025 undefined Act, 2013 has been filed.
6. This Court in Karsanbhai Bhagwanbhai & Ors. v. Dy. Collector and Special Land Acquisition Officer, Narmada - 2011 (3) GLH 702 had the occasion to deal with the similar issue.

entities.text: Karsanbhai Bhagwanbhai & Ors. v. Dy. Collector and Special Land Acquisition Officer, Narmada - 2011 (3) GLH 702
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was observed thus:-
"11.

At this juncture, it may be pertinent to refer to Section 149 of the Code, which makes provision for power to make up deficiency of Court fees, and reads thus:-
"149. Power to make up deficiency of Court-fees.

- Where the whole or any part of any fee prescribed for any document by the law for the time being in force relating to Court-fees has not been paid, the Court may, in its discretion, at any stage, allow the person, by whom such fee is payable, to pay the whole or part, as the case may be, of such Court-fee, and upon such payment the document, in respect of which such fee is payable, shall have the same force and effect as if such fee had been paid in the first instance.

12. A careful reading of Section 149 of the Code shows that where if the Court fee due on the plaint, when instituted, is not paid wholly or partly by the person instituting the suit, the Court in its discretion, may allow him to pay the Court fee or deficit Court fee within the period fixed by it.

The Section further raises a legal fiction in Vaghela Jenubha Jasmatsang vs State Of Gujarat on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149947179/
2 terms whereof as and when such deficit Court fee is paid, the same would be deemed to have been paid in the first instance.

entities.text: Vaghela Jenubha Jasmatsang vs State Of Gujarat on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, merely because Court fees have not been paid at the first instance is no ground for rejecting the reference applications,
inasmuch as by virtue of the provisions of Section 149 of the Code, there is a discretion vested in the Court to allow the applicants to pay such Court fees.

13. In the facts of the present case, it is an admitted position that at the time when the reference applications were submitted to the respondent, both the respective parties were under the impression that no Court fees are payable thereon.

Subsequently that the Government, pursuant to a decision of this High Court issued a Circular instructing all the Land Acquisition Officers to levy ad- valorem Court fees on applications for references u/s 18 of the Act as per Item No. 15 of Schedule I of the Gujarat Court Fees Act, 2004.
It is only thereafter, that the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12952/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/10/2025 undefined respondent called upon the applicants to pay the Court fees.
it is the case of the respondent that the applicants had not paid the Court fees within the time stipulated by him.
However, as noted hereinabove, no order had been made by the respondent rejecting the applications made by the applicants on the ground of non-payment of Court fees.
In fact it appears that before any such order could be made by the respondent, the applicants had moved applications praying for extension of the time for payment of the Court fees.
In the circumstances, it was always permissible for the respondent to extend the time limit by resorting to the provisions of Section 149 of the Code.

However, the respondent, has taken a very hyper technical view of the matter and without assigning any reasons whatsoever as to why the request made by the applicants should not be accepted, has turned down the application for extension of the time limit merely on the ground that the references have been filed (disposed of),
without adverting to any orders having been made whereby the applications of the applicants have in fact been rejected.

14. In Special Civil Application No. 3493 of 2010, the Division Bench was dealing with a case where the application u/s 18 of the Act was refused on the ground that the petitioner had not paid necessary Court fees, as required under the provisions of the Gujarat Court Fees Act, 2004.

In the facts of the said case, the petitioner therein had refused to pay the Court fees under the impression and legal advice to the effect that the earlier judgement of the apex Court and the judgment of this Court rendered before the coming into force the Gujarat Court Fees Act, 2004, would apply in the facts of the case and that the petitioner was in fact not required to pay any Court fees on the application for making the reference.
The petitioner therein submitted that he would pay the necessary Court fees.

The Division Bench, therefore, set aside the order impugned in the said petition whereby the reference application made by the petitioner therein had been rejected, on condition that the petitioner shall affix necessary Court fees within a period of 15 days and his application for making the reference may be reconsidered on that basis for making a reference."

3 7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, it is specifically averred in ground (C) of the writ petition that the petitioner is ready and willing to pay the court fees if the reference of the petitioner is restored.

Learned counsel at the time of hearing has also NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12952/2025 ORDER DATED:
06/10/2025 undefined reiterated that the requisite court fees shall be paid by the petitioner as per the requirement of Article 15 of the Schedule-I of the Gujarat Court Fees Act, 2004 ["Act, 2004" for short].

8. In view of the aforesaid statement and without going into the merits of the claim, as the rejection of the reference application has a far reaching civil consequences in as much as the petitioner will lose his right to just and proper amount of compensation, the impugned order dated 30.09.2024 is quashed and set aside to the extent that the petitioner is permitted to revive the reference application under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 filed by him on deposit of requisite court fees as per Article 15 of the Schedule-I of the Act, 2004.
The petitioner is directed to appear before the respondent No.2 on 03.11.2025 at 3:00 p.m.
The respondent No.2 shall thereafter calculate the requisite court fees payable by the petitioner and intimate the same to the petitioner accordingly by written communication.

Upon receipt of such communication, the petitioner shall pay the court fees within a period of 2 weeks from NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/12952/2025 ORDER DATED:
06/10/2025 undefined the date of receipt of such communication.
Upon payment of such requisite court fees, the respondent No.2 is directed to take further steps expeditiously.
With the aforesaid directions, the present Special Civil Application stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.
Direct Service is permitted.

(ANIRUDDHA P. MAYEE, J.) KAUSHIK D. CHAUHAN Vaghela Jenubha Jasmatsang vs State Of Gujarat on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149947179/
